title: Title

inspiredBy.title: Exact title of the write-up
inspiredBy.note: One or two sentences: what happened for real, and which part of this challenge it maps to. Required (at least one). Shown on the score screen when the player is done.

evidence.label: example.yml
evidence.note: What this file is, in one line.

questions.prompt: A question with exactly one checkable answer.

hints.text: A nudge toward the right area.
The technique, query or tool to use.
Most of the method, stopping short of the answer.
hints.query: optional: the exact explorer query for this tier. It gets a Run in Logs button, and the build checks that it parses and returns rows.

guide.text: Walkthrough step 1 (Guided → Walkthrough mode): what to look at and why. Shown one step at a time.
Step 2: a step can carry a query, which the player runs into Logs with one click.
Last step: point at where the answer is visible, without stating it.

questions.prompt: Pick-one question. Every wrong option explains why it's wrong; the player loses wrongCost per wrong pick and that option is struck out.

options.why: Shown once solved: why this is the best choice, with timestamps or evidence.
Why it's wrong (fires too late, fires on benign data, wouldn't see this at all…). Phrase it as a hint, not the answer.

guide.text: Walkthrough steps are required on every question. For choice and rank questions, explain the reasoning to apply; a query is optional.

questions.prompt: Ranking question, played on its own board tab: the player drags every item into an ordered plan or into Don't do.

items.text: The action that must come first.
items.why: Why it matters. Shown if the player puts it in Don't do, and beside the tile once the question is over.

items.text: The action that must come last.
A tempting action that's wrong here.
items.why: Why it's wrong. Shown if the player puts it in the plan.

rules.why: Shown if broken. Explain the principle without naming the fix outright.
